Notes in the right margin are partly cut off and mostly illegible.

main_text.p: corporis superficiem diffusa. Bilis, à sanguine non segregatus, diffundit se per totum corpus, aut quia hepar excrementum hoc in vesiculam expellere non potest ; aut, ut alii volunt, quia vesicula ad se non trahit. contingit sæpe vitio alimentorum magnam bilis copiam generari : nonnunquam etiam vitio ipsius hepatis nimium calidi. At Ꝼlterus niger est livi-dus corporis color, genitus à succo melancholico in summam cutem effuso, eodem modo, quo in flavo ; nisi quod hic lien male habet sicut vesicula fellis illic. Huc pertinet scorbutus ( Plinii Scelerytbe ) vitiosus corporis habitus, cum crurum debilitate, maculis lividis, gingivis tumidis, sanguinolentis ; ortus a melancholicis succis ; lienis, non satis attrahentis vitio, lien sæpe hic obstruitur, vigorque animi, & alacritas pereunt.
main_text.head: CAP. IX. De Morbis Renum & Vesicæ, &c.
main_text.p: REnum munus est serum à sanguine segregare, & ad vesicā mittere.

page.notes: Right margin notes are cut off by the gutter and largely illegible; not transcribed. The running head and the opening word of the chapter paragraph are set in large initials. Some words in the text are doubtful: "Ꝼlterus" (Icterus) and "lien" and the broken word "Scele-tyrbe" may be misread; the left-page text is in the scan's ink fading near the gutter.
